published_prior_art.cite: Artstein1983 gives general selection-capacity characterizations and LaiRobbins1976 gives the common-marginal extremal maximum coupling, but neither is the stated heterogeneous finite maximum-law formulation.
GreseleEtAl2022 studies global categorical-SCM compatibility through response functions, but does not settle the proposed SMART tree-diagonal projection or its first missing facet.
Shahn2026Oracle proves sharp binary endpoints and compatible lower/upper CDF envelopes, not equality between all discrete oracle pmfs in a recursive polytope and complete FFRCISTG completions.
Russell2021 supplies generic random-set/linear-program sharp-bound machinery; the claimed laminar tree-sized extended formulation is a model-specific computational refinement.
Shahn2026Oracle establishes simultaneous attainability of the two envelope CDFs but does not characterize interior CDF compatibility or exhibit an open nonrectangularity region.
HuangEtAl2017 treats sharp ordinal-treatment-benefit bounds and nonregular inference; multinomial inversion of a fixed sharp polytope is principally a consequence of the proposed projection result.
Shahn2026Oracle Theorem 1 gives the sharp binary oracle interval; this proposition is correctly framed as a required compatibility reduction rather than a novelty claim.

soundness_flags.label: ass:known-randomization and ass:sequential-exchangeability
soundness_flags.one_line: The nodewise conditional equalities quantify over every legal history although a finite SMART law may assign P(H=h)=0; state randomization as joint-kernel equalities (and exchangeability/factorization via specified versions or reached histories) so the completion class is defined on zero-reach branches.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper proves sharp binary oracle endpoints under consistency, sequential exchangeability, positivity, and FFRCISTG, then constructs compatible lower and upper CDF envelope distributions; Appendix A associates incompatible action subtrees while preserving their branch distributions.
The article characterizes distributions of random-set selections by marriage-problem-type inequalities and establishes convex compactness of the resulting family.

source_verification_receipts.version: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 73(2), 1976, pp. 286-288
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: For variables with a common marginal F, the paper defines maximal dependence through the simultaneous maximum-survival law P(max X_i>x)=min{1,n[1-F(x)]}.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Working-paper description of the FFRCISTG/SWIG model
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The source presents SWIGs as a representation of FFRCISTG single-world counterfactual models and their factorization/modularity properties.
The paper formalizes categorical structural causal marginal compatibility using response functions and studies joint SCMs counterfactually consistent with supplied marginal SCMs.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Business and Economic Statistics 39(2), 2021, pp. 532-546
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article develops sharp bounds for continuous functionals of joint potential-outcome distributions using random-set, convex-optimization, and linear-program tools, with computational considerations discussed explicitly.
The paper characterizes sharp scalar identified-set endpoints by optimal-transport problems and proposes dual sample analogues that are root-n consistent with limiting distributions.
The article studies ordinal randomized-trial benefit fractions, proves sharp bounds, and develops a consistent linear-program-based estimator in a setting where naive plug-in estimation can fail.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace all null-history conditional statements by joint randomization equalities or explicitly supplied stochastic kernels, and formulate SWIG conditional kernels only up to an agreed version on dormant/zero-probability parent fibers.

Make the nonrectangularity exhibit a self-contained certificate: calculate the envelope coordinates for P-star, verify q-star is strictly interior, and display the particular tree-capacity inequality that excludes it; then state the perturbation argument yielding the open positive-law region.

Keep projection-and-lift as the single field-tier headline and label the compact-LP and finite-sample inversion results as corollaries conditional on it; add a second dynamic-oracle comparator only if pursuing a higher-tier comparator-frontier claim.

recommended_next_step: Revise the zero-reach conditional-kernel formulation, retain the complete FFRCISTG lift as the field-tier solve target, and then advance to Stage 0.
